A.title: Document structure

items.label: Approved words
items.sub: UPPERCASE: one meaning, one part of speech

items.label: Technical nouns
items.sub: the names your field uses for things

items.label: Technical verbs
items.sub: the verbs your field uses for actions

A.note: A rule number names its section: rule 5.1 is in section 5. Section 9 also gives 8 general recommendations (GR-1 to GR-8).

B.title: Anatomy of STE sentences

original.label: Original text, not STE: words to replace are in red
original.text: It is imperative that the operator ensures the cache files are purged prior to commencing the update.

marks.tip: rule 4.1 · say it as a command
rule 1.1 · ensure is not approved → MAKE SURE
rule 3.6 · passive; purge is not approved → REMOVE
rule 1.1 · prior to is not approved → BEFORE
rules 1.1 + 3.5 · commence → START, and no -ing verb

items.heading: Procedural sentence: the same instruction, rewritten
items.ste: Make sure that you remove the cache files before you start the update.

items.heading: Safety instruction
items.ste: CAUTION: Do not stop the server during the update. If you stop it, the data can become incorrect.

spans.note: caution = risk of damage · warning = risk of injury

spans.text: Do not stop the server during the update.
If you stop it, the data can become incorrect.

items.heading: Descriptive sentence
items.ste: The scheduler starts the backup at 02:00 UTC.

B.foot: Procedural max 20 words · descriptive max 25 words · max 6 sentences per paragraph · one topic per paragraph.

C.title: Verb forms

rows.example: Use the script to stop the server.

C.note: Use the -ing form only inside a technical noun, for example "load balancing". Descriptive text can use the passive only when you do not know who does the action.

D.title: Dictionary entries

rows.good: MAKE SURE THAT the tests pass.
BEFORE you start the update, stop the server.
rows.bad: Prior to the update, stop the server.

rows.good: Send the data THROUGH the proxy.
rows.bad: Send the data via the proxy.

D.note: Approved words are UPPERCASE, words not approved are lowercase. An approved word keeps one meaning and one part of speech. These examples are ours; the full dictionary is a free download from asd-ste100.org.

practices.text: Use the same word for the same thing every time.
Do not leave out words like "the", "a" and "this".
Use the active voice in procedures.
Use vertical lists for complex text.
Write one topic in each paragraph.
Do not use semicolons, contractions or phrasal verbs.

F.title: History

points.text: European airlines ask AECMA to make maintenance texts easier to read
The AECMA Simplified English Working Group starts

F.note: STEMG: the Simplified Technical English Maintenance Group of ASD.
